Incidents Bot: ALERT 1934567890 - Serving runtime: spike in model-load failures across us-west-2 pools. Severity: P1. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
Maya O'Neill: acked. I'm oncall for eng-sre, will triage now.
Maya O'Neill: high level: ~30% of load attempts for model 'open-7b-v2' are failing during warmup with OOM/CUDA errors; upstream requests are getting 5xx and some customers reporting degraded responses.
Sarah Patel: saw the same from tracing — errors start at 1934567885, correlate with a rollout that increased concurrency for warmup jobs.
Liam Chen: I'm runtime eng. Jumping in. Any recent config changes to warmup concurrency or compile timeout?
Maya O'Neill: yes, a policy tweak to bump warmup concurrency from 4 -> 8 went out 1934567600 (canary), then rolled to prod 1934567720.
Maya O'Neill: logs attached below.
Maya O'Neill: ```
[2026-03-15T12:31:04Z] load_model: loading open-7b-v2 shard-2
[2026-03-15T12:31:04Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc failed, out of memory (requested 4.00 GiB)
[2026-03-15T12:31:04Z] warmup: deserialization error: invalid tensor header at offset 0x1a2f
[2026-03-15T12:31:04Z] compile: nvrtc compile timed out after 30s
[2026-03-15T12:31:04Z] container: oom-killed process pid=12134
```
Carlos Ruiz: customer-impact: CS reported two mid-market customers seeing increased 5xx and higher latency on batch endpoints; estimated retries causing user-visible errors. No major revenue-impacting customers yet but a few active sessions disrupted.
Maya O'Neill: immediate mitigations I'm doing: 1) toggle warmup concurrency policy back to 4 for us-west-2 via feature flag, 2) add temporary routing rule to divert new loads to fallback model variant open-7b-v2-quant (smaller, 8-bit) for latency-sensitive customers, 3) start rolling restart of affected node pool to clear stuck containers.
Liam Chen: concur. Also propose increasing the compile timeout to 90s for the hot path and disable parallel JIT for now. Command I ran in prod config: `kubectl patch cm runtime-config -n redwood --type merge -p '{"data":{"JIT_PARALLEL": "false", "NVRTC_TIMEOUT_S": "90"}}'`
Sarah Patel: I'm increasing alert throttle to avoid noisy repeats and marking these metrics as suppression while we stabilize.
DevOps Bot: Runbook step executed: scaled nodepool "inference-usw2-1" +2 nodes, started graceful drain for flapping instance ip-10-0-12-45.
Maya O'Neill: status update 1934567950: warmup concurrency flag rolled back, fallback routing enabled for two customers, immediate error rate dropped from 32% -> 7% for new loads. Old pending warmup attempts still failing while OOM state clears.
Liam Chen: I'm attaching a small script to clear the compile cache on nodes before restarting runtime: `ssh node && rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/compile-cache/* && systemctl restart redwood-runtime` — running on one node as canary.
Maya O'Neill: can we confirm whether deserialization error is due to a corrupted checkpoint or streaming deserialiser change?
Liam Chen: preliminary grep suggests a partial checkpoint write coincident with a node crash (oom-kill). There's a pattern: shard files truncated to size 0x1a2f. We'll trigger integrity check for recent shard writes.
Sarah Patel: telemetry: node flaps show sudden memory usage jumps from 60% -> 98% during parallel warmup spikes. Looks like concurrent warmup tasks are exceeding host GPU memory when several heavy shards start at once.
Carlos Ruiz: CS: customers want ETA. I told them mitigation in place and asked for 1hr ETA for stabilization, customer-facing note pending until we confirm full recovery.
Maya O'Neill: quick ask for support teams: please hold any non-urgent model uploads that trigger warmup. I'll post when safe to resume.
Liam Chen: long-term proposals noted in thread: - enforce serialized shard load per-GPU during warmup (no concurrency above 1 per-GPU for big models), - add pre-warm memory checks and backoff, - atomic checkpoint writes with rename to prevent truncated deserializations, - increase default NVRTC timeout for complex kernels.
DevOps Bot: Handoff reminder: oncall shift change in 40m. Maya handing to Liam at end of shift unless resolved.
Maya O'Neill: handing to Liam: summary — root cause likely concurrent warmup jobs causing GPU mem pressure leading to cuMemAlloc OOM and partial checkpoint deserializations; mitigation applied: warmup concurrency rolled back, fallback variant routing, nodepool nodes added, compile timeout increased, rolling restarts in progress. Error rate trending down.
Liam Chen: taking over oncall. I'll document actions in the incident tracker and keep CS updates every 15m. Starting full nodefile integrity scan now.
Maya O'Neill: thanks — I'll stay available for context.
DevOps Bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1934567890, severity P1, assigned to Liam Chen.
Carlos Ruiz: will follow up with customers and send a short status note: "We have applied mitigations; some customers are routed to a smaller model. We're monitoring, ETA 1 hour to full recovery."
Liam Chen: status 1934568025: integrity scan done on canary node — found 3 truncated shard writes; quarantined those files, re-pulled replicas from object store, reloaded successfully. Error rate now 1.2% and falling. Will keep monitoring and then run postmortem checklist.
Sarah Patel: leaving a note to run heap/stack sampling on nodes that were oom-killed to ensure there isn't memory leak in warmup routines.
Maya O'Neill: noted. Moving this to incident follow-up channel for postmortem writeup and RCA once stabilized. Good job team. :thumbsup:
